context.body: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

context.body: Taking, Rebuke, and House Fracture · 2 Samuel 12:26–31
context.label: Canonical location

observations.body: Joab captures the royal city and summons David, who takes the crown, removes spoil, brings out the inhabitants, and puts them to labor before returning to Jerusalem.
observations.label: Rabbah falls and its people are put to labor: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Joab, David, the Ammonite king, Rabbah’s inhabitants, and Israel, Rabbah and Jerusalem, capturing, summoning, gathering, taking a crown and spoil, bringing out people, assigning labor, and returning visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Rabbah falls and its people are put to labor: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Joab, David, the Ammonite king, Rabbah’s inhabitants, and Israel · Rabbah and Jerusalem · capturing, summoning, gathering, taking a crown and spoil, bringing out people, assigning labor, and returning · the war left in chapter 11 closes with conquest and coerced labor
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 12:26–31

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 12:26–31 as its own taking, rebuke, and house fracture David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the war left in chapter 11 closes with conquest and coerced labor inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Rabbah falls and its people are put to labor
